Subject: Re: Customer incident pattern - P2 delays overnight (APAC)

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from my ops team: over the last three weeks we've seen multiple P2s open overnight that stayed >6 hours without a triage. The issues are intermittent (edge replication + increased tokenization cost) but our users are sensitive to the latency.

We understand Redwood has limited overnight on-call coverage for our plan, but can we request a temporary contingency for the next six weeks while we complete our migration? Specifically: a documented standby (named on-call backup), a committed P2 response window of 4 hours (weekend nights APAC), and an explicit escalation ladder to a senior on-call if triage isn't acknowledged in 4 hours.

We'd appreciate confirmation and a runbook we can reference in our incident playbooks. If needed, we can sign an amendment to the SLA.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability
AcmeCloud

Thanks for the detailed note and the incident samples, Elena. We take this seriously.

Proposed short-term plan (6-week window) — simple, operational, and auditable:
- Temporary P2 response SLA: 4-hour acknowledged triage for weekend APAC P2s (exception to standard business-hours policy).
- Standby roster: Redwood will designate a named backup (rotating) who is paged immediately for APAC overnight P2s.
- Escalation ladder: 0-4h triage -> if no ack, escalate to senior on-call -> 2h later notify CS/SE to coordinate workaround.

I'll attach a draft runbook and the SLA amendment text for legal to review. If this looks acceptable I'll ask Camila to confirm operational feasibility and Ben to propose the rotation names.

Next steps:
1) Camila to confirm operational acceptance and capacity.
2) Ben to propose rotation schedule (names & contact numbers).
3) Draft amendment routed to Acme legal for signature (DocuSign link).

I can hop on a quick call today at 3pm PT if that's useful.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
